arguments.message: Beacon Works initial plan: Considering assigning my irrigation pump (machine_007: 8-12, 2.4kW/h) to src_Biomass. For 8-12h pump, src_Biomass has 1.7kW capacity which should handle my 2.4kW needs if no one else is using heavily during those hours. What's your plan?

However, I also have afternoon demand 13-19 (2.9kW) and late evening 21-24 (3.8kW). Given the Biomass capacity dips in afternoon/evening, I'm considering splitting my assignments. How are others planning to use the afternoon/evening Biomass capacity? Also, with only me on Hydro, I might use that for some of my early morning load to reduce Biomass pressure.

Aurora Industries checking in. I see you have irrigation pump 8-12h (2.4kW) planning to use Biomass. I have machines 7-12h totaling 6.4kW (water heater 1.6kW + HVAC 3.2kW + HVAC 1.6kW). The Biomass capacity 7-12 is only 0.4-1.7kW, so we definitely have a conflict. I'm considering using my exclusive Wind access for part of my 7-12 load. Could you potentially shift your irrigation pump to your exclusive Geothermal source to free up Biomass capacity for both of us?

Beacon Works here. After analyzing capacities more carefully, I see the conflicts are worse than initially thought. For my 8-12h irrigation pump (2.4kW): Biomass can only provide 1.2-1.7kW during those hours, and my exclusive Geothermal provides even less (1.4kW dropping to 0.6kW). Neither source can handle my full 2.4kW load alone. I'm considering splitting this machine's assignment - perhaps using Biomass for the 8-10 portion and accepting some overflow, or using Geothermal for partial coverage. For my 0-6h machine (0.9kW), I'll definitely use Geothermal. For 18-20h (2.9kW), Biomass has 2.1-2.7kW which is still short but better than Geothermal's 1.0-1.4kW. How flexible are you with your timing windows?

Beacon Works update: The capacity constraints are tighter than expected. For my irrigation pump (8-12h, 2.4kW), even my exclusive Geothermal can't handle it (max 1.4kW at 8-9, drops to 0.6kW by 11-12). Biomass is also insufficient (1.2-1.7kW). I'm planning to: (1) Use Geothermal for my 0-6h refrigeration (0.9kW) - fits easily. (2) For 8-12h pump: will likely need to accept some overflow regardless of source choice, but Biomass seems slightly better. (3) For 18-20h refrigeration (2.9kW): Biomass capacity is 2.1-2.7kW, so minimal overflow. Cascade Labs - given your heavy 3-6 Biomass needs, I won't conflict there. Aurora - we both have timing flexibility issues in the 7-12 window. Should we coordinate who uses which source when?

Cascade Labs update: Given the tight Biomass constraints, I'm revising my strategy. For 3-6 window: I'll put my Water heater (1.6kW) on Hydro since I have exclusive access there, and split my remaining 4.6kW (Server rack + EV charger) between Biomass and accepting some overflow. This reduces my Biomass demand during your critical periods. For 13-19 afternoon: My 2.9kW total (Kiln 1.3kW + CNC mill 1.6kW) vs Biomass capacity 0-1.5kW means significant overflow regardless. For 21-24: My 3.8kW Server rack vs 1.2-2.4kW Biomass capacity also means overflow. Aurora/Beacon - should we coordinate who takes the limited afternoon Biomass capacity, or should I plan to accept overflow on my afternoon/evening machines and leave the Biomass for your more flexible loads?

Cascade Labs here. I see we both have access to Solar source. Looking at Solar capacity, it's very limited and only really available 7-11 and 14-15. I don't have any machines that fit well in those windows - my demand is 3-6, 13-19, and 21-24. Are you planning to use Solar for any of your machines? I want to make sure I'm not missing a coordination opportunity here.
